extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users creating graphics with TikZ/pgf (authors of technical documents, plots, and diagrams)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and option semantics for producing tree edges, plots, plot marks, smoothing, external-function plots (gnuplot), coordinate systems, and coordinate transformations in TikZ/pgf. Covers when to use TikZ for plots and practical warnings/options for reliable rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: edge from parent default insertion
rubrics_metrics.description: The edge-from-parent operation essentially inserts the path segment (\tikzparentnode) -- (\tikzchildnode), i.e., an edge from the parent to the child. The macros \tikzparentnode and \tikzchildnode expand to the names of the parent/child nodes even if no explicit name was assigned (an internal name is auto-generated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can modify the inserted edge-from-parent path to change appearance (e.g., draw a curve instead of a straight line).

rubrics_metrics.name: customizing edge-from-parent path
rubrics_metrics.description: You may replace the default straight line inserted by edge from parent with any path (e.g., a Bézier curve via controls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: set edge from parent path to { (\tikzparentnode.south) .. controls +(0,-1) and +(0,1) .. (\tikzchildnode.north) } to draw curved edges.

rubrics_metrics.name: child anchor option
rubrics_metrics.description: child anchor=(anchor) sets the anchor where the edge from parent meets the child node by setting macro \tikzchildanchor to .(anchor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you specify border as the anchor, \tikzchildanchor is set to the empty string and the edge meets the child's border at an automatically calculated position.

rubrics_metrics.name: parent anchor option
rubrics_metrics.description: parent anchor=(anchor) works the same way as child anchor but for the parent node (sets \tikzparentanchor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to control the attachment point of the parent end of the inserted edge.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=edge from parent insertion and redefinition
rubrics_metrics.description: The edge-from-parent operation installs the style=edge from parent prior to inserting the edge-from-parent path; by default this style just draws the edge from parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can redefine style=edge from parent (e.g., \tikzstyle{edge from parent}=[draw,red,thick]) to change the default drawing of all such edges.

rubrics_metrics.name: options inserted before edge-from-parent apply to whole child path
rubrics_metrics.description: The options inserted before the edge-from-parent path are added to the whole child path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently, you cannot, for example, draw a circle in red as part of the child path and then have an edge to parent in blue via these options. The child node itself (being a node) can still be drawn differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: edge-from-parent affects node placement (pos semantics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The edge-from-parent operation causes all nodes following the operation to be placed on the edge; this is the same effect as adding the pos option to those nodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., child {node {} edge to parent node {label}} behaves like (root) -- (child) node[pos=0.5]{label}.

rubrics_metrics.name: edge-to-parent equivalence with manual path
rubrics_metrics.description: An edge to parent operation combined with a following node is equivalent to inserting a path and a node with pos, e.g., (root) -- (child) node[pos=0.5]{label}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this equivalence to reason about labels and positions on edges when combining child/parent operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: when to use TikZ for plots (advantages vs external programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikZ may be preferred over externally produced plots when you need fonts, formulas, line widths, ticks, arrows/plot marks, and scaling to match the document, and to avoid automatic 'chart junk' and mismatched styling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External programs often use different fonts, render formulas differently (or not at all), produce mismatched line widths, scale oddly when included, generate distracting grids/ticks, and create chart junk; TikZ keeps visuals consistent with the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: plot path operation forms (--plot vs plot)
rubrics_metrics.description: \path ... --plot{further arguments} continues the current (sub)path by implicitly adding a line-to to the first point; \path ... plot{further arguments} moves to the first coordinate of the curve before plotting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose --plot when you want to continue the path from the last point; use plot when the plot should be a separate subpath.

rubrics_metrics.name: ways to specify plot data
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot coordinates can be specified inline (coordinates list), read from an external file (file{filename}), computed via a coordinate expression, or via function{gnuplot formula}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each method has local options and differing preprocessing behavior (e.g., function uses gnuplot or pgf math engine).

rubrics_metrics.name: inline coordinate plot format
rubrics_metrics.description: Inline plotting uses syntax like \draw plot coordinates {(0,0) (1,1) ...}; the operation will connect or smooth according to options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use --plot vs plot to control whether a line-to to the first coordinate is added implicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: external file format for plots
rubrics_metrics.description: TikZ expects external plot files where each line starts with two numbers separated by a space; anything after the two numbers is ignored; lines starting with % or # and empty lines are ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the format produced by gnuplot's 'set terminal table'. You can produce such files yourself for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: local plot options are local to each plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Local options passed to plot (e.g., plot[yshift=1cm]) affect only that plot and not other plots on the same path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, most styling options apply to the entire path as a whole; e.g., plot[red] will not locally make only the plotted part red if path styling rules prevent per-segment color application.

rubrics_metrics.name: plot coordinate expression and variable option
rubrics_metrics.description: When plotting a function via a coordinate expression, use a special macro (\x by default) whose value is varied. The variable option can change which macro is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expressions sometimes need braces around x- or y-coordinates when using parentheses inside the math expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: plot sampling options (samples, domain, samples at)
rubrics_metrics.description: samples=number sets number of samples (default 25); domain=start:end sets sampling domain (default -5:5); samples at={list} forces evaluation at specified positions and overrules samples/domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use samples at to specify explicit sample points (\foreach syntax allowed). Precedence: samples at overrides samples and domain; setting samples or domain overrules samples at in the other direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotting using gnuplot requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To use plot function{...} that calls gnuplot, two conditions must be met: (1) TeX must be allowed to call external programs (shell-escape/enable-write18), and (2) gnuplot must be installed and locatable by TeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these are not met, TikZ can still produce .gnuplot files on first run and you can run gnuplot by hand to produce .table files. Provide unique ids to plots to ease redistribution and avoid regenerating tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: TikZ gnuplot workflow and caching (.gnuplot/.table/id/prefix)
rubrics_metrics.description: On first encounter TikZ writes a .gnuplot file (\jobnameid.gnuplot) and expects gnuplot to produce a .table file; on subsequent runs, if .table exists and .gnuplot appears unchanged, TikZ will read the .table without calling gnuplot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use id= to give unique identifiers to plots (improves sharing and compilation speed). Use prefix= to change output directory/filename prefix. raw gnuplot passes commands directly to gnuplot.

rubrics_metrics.name: gnuplot syntax for function plots (x vs parametric t)
rubrics_metrics.description: When using plot function{gnuplot formula}, use x as the variable for normal plots and t for parametric plots (parametric=true requires two comma-separated functions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For complicated uses, prefer external gnuplot generator files and include the resulting table files; raw gnuplot allows passing set samples, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every plot
rubrics_metrics.description: style=every plot is installed in each plot (as if you always said plot[style=every plot,...]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \tikzstyle{every plot}=[prefix=plots/] or similar to globally set a prefix or other options for all plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: mark option and declared plot marks
rubrics_metrics.description: mark=(mark mnemonic) places a copy of the declared plot mark at every plot point. Default marks: *, +, x; more marks available via pgflibraryplotmarks; the 'ball' mark is special and only available in TikZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ball marks can be slow in PostScript (avoid with many marks). Define custom marks via \pgfdeclareplotmark.

rubrics_metrics.name: mark repeat, mark phase, mark indices
rubrics_metrics.description: mark repeat=r draws only every r-th mark; mark phase=p sets which mark is drawn first (p-th, then p+r,...); mark indices=list explicitly lists indices (1-based) at which marks are drawn (\foreach syntax allowed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these options to control mark density and alignment with sampled data.

rubrics_metrics.name: mark size and mark options
rubrics_metrics.description: mark size=dimension sets size of plot marks (for circles it's the radius; for others about half width/height); mark options={...} applies style to marks when drawn (color, rotation, scale, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can achieve the same sizing via a local scale, but mark size is faster and more natural. mark options can transform or color marks independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: marks drawn after path (marks like text nodes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Marks are placed after the whole path has been drawn/filled/shaded; marks are handled like text nodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of z-order: marks will overlay the path content since they are drawn after the path.

rubrics_metrics.name: sharp vs smooth vs tension and smoothing caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: sharp plot (default) connects points by straight lines. smooth connects points with smooth curves. tension=value controls how 'tight' smoothing is (default 0.55; lower -> sharper corners, higher -> rounder curves).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smoothing algorithm is simple: best results when bending angles are small (less than ~30°) and point spacing is roughly uniform. A tension of 1 yields a circle for four quarter-circle points.

rubrics_metrics.name: smooth cycle and equivalent cycle construction
rubrics_metrics.description: smooth cycle connects plot points using a closed smooth curve. The same effect can be achieved by plotting coordinates then using -- cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use smooth cycle for closed smooth shapes; compare behavior to explicit cycle if you need precise control.

rubrics_metrics.name: comb plot types (ycomb, xcomb, polar comb)
rubrics_metrics.description: ycomb: for each point add a straight line from x-axis to the point (vertical 'comb' or bar diagram). xcomb: horizontal variant. polar comb: line from origin to each polar-coordinate point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for bar/comb style plots; combine with mark options to style endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: only marks option
rubrics_metrics.description: only marks causes only plot marks to be shown; no path segments are added to the path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for scatter-plot-like overlays or to add marks to an existing path without connecting lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: coordinate transformation chain and accessible systems
rubrics_metrics.description: A coordinate goes through several transforms before final placement (xy-coordinate interpretation, coordinate transformation matrix, backend/page transforms, canvas transforms, device transforms). TikZ/pgf exposes only the xy-coordinate system and the coordinate transformation matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not modify the canvas transformation matrix unless you know what you are doing—doing so makes pgf lose track of coordinates, anchors, and bounding box computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: xy/xyz-coordinate system semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: A coordinate (x,y) means x*vx + y*vy where vx and vy are the current x- and y-vectors; (x,y,z) extends to vz. Unlike many packages, vx need not be horizontal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because x-vector can point anywhere, mixed coordinates like (1,2pt) are not supported. Use x=, y=, z= options to alter the basis vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: setting x,y,z vector options
rubrics_metrics.description: x=dimension sets the x-vector to (dimension,0); x=(coordinate) sets x-vector to specified coordinate (use braces if coordinate contains a comma). y= and z= work analogously (z dimension interpreted as (value,value)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to change the meaning/direction/scale of coordinate axes (e.g., swap x and y by x={(0cm,1cm)},y={(1cm,0cm)}).

rubrics_metrics.name: coordinate transformation matrix applies only to coordinates
rubrics_metrics.description: The coordinate transformation matrix affects coordinates only; it does not affect non-coordinate attributes such as line width, dash patterns, or shading angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General rule: if no 'coordinate' is involved, the matrix is not applied. When in doubt, test or consult documentation for whether a dimension is transformed.

rubrics_metrics.name: transformations are local and immediate
rubrics_metrics.description: Transformations are added via graphic options and are local to the current TeX group; they apply immediately when encountered 'in the middle of a path' and affect only coordinates following the transformation option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this behavior to position things relative to transformed coordinate frames, and remember transforms are scoped.

rubrics_metrics.name: basic transform options and their effects
rubrics_metrics.description: shift={(coordinate)} adds the coordinate to all coordinates; shift only cancels all current transformations except shifting; xshift=, yshift= add fixed offsets to x/y; scale=, xscale=, yscale= scale coordinates; xslant=, yslant= slant coordinates; rotate= rotates coordinate system; rotate around={deg:(coordinate)} rotates around a point; cm={a,b,c,d,(tx,ty)} applies an arbitrary affine matrix and translation; reset cm resets the matrix to identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rotate around to rotate about a point. reset cm is dangerous (destroys inherited transforms); cm is rarely needed unless you require arbitrary affine transforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid aggressive scaling and matrix singularities
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use very large or near-zero scaling factors; TeX has low numeric accuracy and some operations require inverting the transformation matrix, which can fail if the matrix is badly conditioned or singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don't understand singular matrices, avoid extreme transforms. Use modest scaling and test compiled results.

rubrics_metrics.name: loading arrow tip library
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \usepgflibrary{arrows} or \usetikzlibrary{arrows} to load the arrow-tip library which defines additional arrow tips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrow names containing '<' or '>' are left undefined for the user to define; see arrow library documentation for tip names and thick/thin variants.
